newsitem.title: USA: Sears, Roebuck & Co targets 15 pct EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Sears, Roebuck & Co targets 15 pct EPS growth.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck & Co aims for 15 percent growth in earnings per share but expects that its department store unit will slightly exceed that this year, chief financial officer Alan Lacy said.
Sears' department stores make up about two-thirds of its business.

Sears also sees its total number of stores of all types doubling between 1995 and the year 2000 to total about 5,000 stores including both specialty categories and department stores, said Lacy, who is also an executive vice president. He spoke at the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference.
Montgomery Securities analyst Tom Tashjian predicts Sears' earnings will grow 18 percent in 1996 and in 1997. Lacy would not comment on Montgomery's earnings projections for the company.

Sears is pursuing a growth strategy focused on home and home improvement categories and on auto parts categories. It has an aggressive expansion plan for its specialty stores which include HomeLife furniture store, Western Auto auto parts, Sears Hardware stores and others.
But another over-riding strategy is increasing apparel sales within its department stores, since apparel has proved to be a growth source at the department stores.
Lacy said apparel now constitutes 62 percent of its department store selling space, up from 55 percent about two years ago.
